description: Outlier detection painted into the Svelte 5 data grid. A background pass computes per-column anomalies, IQR distance for numeric columns with warning, outlier and extreme thresholds at 1.5, 3 and 6 times the interquartile range, and rare-value detection for low-cardinality categoricals seen in under 2 percent of rows. The cell snippet paints a coloured halo by severity and a tooltip explaining which rule fired; the whole map is one $derived, so cells read it in constant time and sorting or filtering never triggers a rescan.

faq.question: How are outliers detected?
faq.answer: For each numeric column the quartiles are computed once and every value is scored by its distance from the interquartile range. Categorical columns flag values that appear in fewer than 2 percent of rows.

faq.question: How is the severity shown?
faq.answer: The cell snippet reads the score from the anomaly map and adds a warning, outlier or extreme class that draws a halo; the tooltip names the detector and the threshold that tripped.

faq.question: Does the scan run on every render?
faq.answer: No. The map is a $derived of the data, so it recomputes only when rows change; sorting and filtering just re-read it.
